title: Chapo Launches Pró-Jovem Youth Financing Programme
summary: President Chapo announced the launch of Pró-Jovem in Pemba, Cabo Delgado, replacing the Fund for Support to Youth Initiatives (FAIJ) to expand financing for youth projects across all districts. The programme will operate along the lines of PRO-MULHER and FDEL. Chapo also announced the government would double the value of its programme contract with the National Youth Council.

title: France and Holland Reaffirm Economic Cooperation with Mozambique
summary: The ambassadors of France and Holland met with President Chapo as their diplomatic missions draw to a close. The Dutch ambassador highlighted maritime logistics and the Beira and Nacala development corridors as key areas for cooperation. The French ambassador pointed to bilateral cooperation in energy, cultural industries, defense, and regional cooperation in the Mozambique Channel.

title: Chapo Condemns Xenophobic Violence at SADC Summit
summary: Speaking after the 46th SADC Summit in Durban, Chapo said violence will never resolve migration-related conflicts between peoples who share the same history. He noted Ramaphosa reiterated his apology and offered condolences to bereaved families. Chapo called for strengthening SADC's role in promoting safe migration and urged Mozambicans not to retaliate. On compensation, he said it was premature to discuss while the process is ongoing.

title: Samia to Inaugurate $2.9B Julius Nyerere Hydropower Project
summary: President Samia is expected to officially inaugurate the Julius Nyerere Hydropower Project (JNHPP) on August 22, 2026. The project, with an installed capacity of 2,115 megawatts and an investment of Sh7.45 trillion (~$2.9B), is the largest electricity generation project ever implemented in Tanzania using government funds.

title: Samia and Tshisekedi Deepen Security, Economic Ties
summary: At State House in Zanzibar, Samia and DRC President Tshisekedi called for the withdrawal of foreign forces from Congolese territory and pledged deeper defence cooperation. The talks produced a Strategic Partnership on Minerals covering critical minerals and value addition, commitments to improve Central Corridor transport links through Dar es Salaam, Kigoma and Kalemie, and energy cooperation exploring synergies with EACOP and TAZAMA.

title: Kagame Rejects Burundi President's Claim on Commitments
summary: At an August 24 press conference, Kagame rejected Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye's claim that Rwanda failed to honour commitments, saying "there is no commitment we ever made that we did not fulfill." He recalled an episode where Ndayishimiye denied Burundian troops were deploying to North Kivu, only for them to be captured there weeks later, adding "I don't tell lies like he did to me."

title: Vice President Nchimbi Resigns, Says Samia Wanted Change
summary: Tanzanian Vice President Emmanuel Nchimbi resigned on August 25, saying he had become convinced President Samia wanted a change in the country's second-highest office. He cited a promise made to her on August 27, 2025, that he would leave whenever she felt she needed another vice president, and said he is retiring from politics and public service.

title: Chapo Outlines Seven Theses for FRELIMO's 2027 Congress
summary: Closing the 11th National Conference of Cadres in Chimoio, Chapo announced seven proposed theses for FRELIMO's 13th Congress: National Unity, Peace and Security; Economic Independence; Youth; Women; Democratic Rule of Law and Decentralisation; Party Sustainability; and International Geopolitics. He said counterterrorism must be a national priority, praised Rwandan and Tanzanian forces in Cabo Delgado, and declared "in FRELIMO there is no place for thieves."

title: Mozambique and U.S. Establish Permanent Trade and Investment Framework
summary: Mozambique and the United States announced on August 27 a permanent dialogue mechanism to facilitate trade, promote investment and address obstacles faced by businesses. The framework follows Chapo's October 2025 U.S. visit and is expected to focus heavily on energy, where the U.S. Export-Import Bank is backing Mozambique LNG with up to $4.7 billion and ExxonMobil leads the Rovuma LNG project in Area 4.

title: Tinubu Begins Three-Week Leave, Presidency Silent on Acting President
summary: The presidency announced Tinubu would depart Abuja for Europe to begin a three-week vacation as part of his annual leave, with London as his first stop. Spokesperson Bayo Onanuga was silent on whether power would be transferred to Vice President Kashim Shettima, which would require formally notifying the Senate President. Shettima is in Angola representing Tinubu at the AU leaders summit.
